title: Customer Part Sales tab: Total Price includes tax
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including Part sales -> Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit.
  2. A test customer exists. If not: top menu Customers -> New Customer, enter a Name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and click Save.
  3. A test vendor exists to order parts from. If not: top menu Parts -> Vendors (left sidebar) -> New Vendor, enter a Name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Parts Supply"), pick a value in Taxes (required, e.g. "GST"), then click Save & Close.
  4. Start a new part sale today (a sale started before this release handles cores the old way): top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale; in the New part sale dialog pick the Customer and click Save. The sale opens with the status Estimate.
  5. On the Parts tab click Add Part (on a sale with no parts the Add Part dialog opens by itself). In the Add Part dialog enter Description "Brake Pads", Quantity 1 (required), Vendor = the test vendor and Sell Price $100.00, then click Save & Close.
  6. Set the tax: on the Financial Info card click the edit icon (tooltip "Edit tax rate"), pick an 8.25% rate in the Taxes list and click Save (if none exists, first add "ZZAUTOTEST 8.25%" at 8.25%: click your initials at the top right -> Settings -> Taxes -> New Tax).
  7. Check the sale's own Total on the Finance tab: $108.25 ($100.00 + $8.25 tax).
  8. For comparison, a work order for the same customer with a taxable $100.00 part: top menu Work Orders -> Create Work Order, select the customer, add a line with a part at Sell Price $100.00, tax 8.25%.
custom_steps:
1. Open top menu Customers, open the customer, and on the customer page open the Part Sales tab (it shows a count, e.g. "Part Sales (4)").
  2. Find the seeded part sale and read its Total Price.
  3. Compare it with the sale's own total including tax (e.g. $108.25).
  4. Open the Work Orders tab on the same customer overview and read the work order's Total Price.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The part sale's Total Price on the Part Sales tab includes tax: $108.25 in the example ($100.00 + $8.25 tax), not $100.00.
  • It equals the part sale's own total including tax, to the cent.
  • The Work Orders tab's Total Price includes tax in the same way, so both tabs read alike.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10264 (Change the tax on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569) as edited 5 October 2026, Story 3; read 5 Oct 2026. Source-verified 5 October 2026.
